## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Add support for:
- Dynamic Google Cast groups
- Fetching manufacturer from local API

Dynamic groups will not be added as entities in Home Assistant, but a pychromecast Chromecast object will be created to keep track of media status of the dynamic group, which will then be shown on the group members.

This re-adds functionality which was previously removed by PRs: #34082, #33884, #33845

comments: I updated the youtube video link to the correct link -> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PsO-ECWChog

Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`cast`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L71) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Just to be sure there is no magic going on here, does this happen also if the speaker group is not named "All speakers"?

Please collect and attach a complete log, from start of HA until you have reproduced the issue and a duplicated speaker group entity is created, with these log settings:
```yaml
logger:
  default: info
  logs:
    homeassistant.core: debug
    homeassistant.components.cast: debug
    homeassistant.components.cast.media_player: debug
    pychromecast: debug
    pychromecast.discovery: debug
    pychromecast.socket_client: debug
    homeassistant.components.zeroconf: debug
    zeroconf: info
```

Logs here - actual instance of problem from 19:55 ish:

[home-assistant.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/5213773/home-assistant.zip)

Here is screenshot taken at 19:55 showing one Upstairs speaker group (sorry don't know how to resize screenshots):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/596188/93031959-c9cc1d00-f682-11ea-885f-7ed88f5ac5f3.png)

Then using Google Home android app I 'move' a spotify stream from Living Area to Upstairs and get Upstairs group duplicated, this screenshot taken at 19:56:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/596188/93031998-fa13bb80-f682-11ea-98a1-8a7303228bf8.png)

Both speaker groups contain the same Google Home speakers which may be relevant.

Thanks a lot for the log!

The root cause for the problem is that a temporary speaker group, also named "Upstairs" but with its own UUID, is created when you're moving the stream around. Because UUID is different, Home Assistant sees the temporary speaker group as a new group.
This is very similar to an old feature with Google removed some time ago, PR which removed the support in HA: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/33884

Is the problem 100% reproducible, or does it only happen sometimes?
You have not by any chance blocked the ChromeCasts from updating themselves?

Can you also try if temporary groups are also formed if you follow this sequence - which is when temporary speaker groups were created with the old feature:
- Start a first stream to a speaker group
- Start a second stream one member of the speaker group.
- The speaker group - except for the one member -  should continue the first stream and a temporary group should be formed.

Re-adding support for temporary groups will require quite a lot of changes.
~~The good news is that the cast now seems to make it clear that a temporary group is formed:~~
Edited: This is not good news.
```
2020-09-13 19:56:37 DEBUG (Thread-23) [pychromecast.socket_client] [Living Area(192.168.86.213):32023] Received: Message urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.multizone from receiver-0 to *: {'changedDevices': [], 'failedDevices': [], 'name': 'Upstairs', 'requestId': 0, 'sessionEndpoint': {'deviceId': '7a583f9c-c7ea-4dde-a042-436135e561e5', 'ipAddress': '192.168.86.213', 'port': 32019, 'sessionId': '79f4f222-4d4b-4a39-bd1d-76ed53d4f1b6'}, 'type': 'PLAYBACK_SESSION_UPDATED'}
```

Probably completely unrelated to this issue, but there may be something fishy with how pychromecast maintains the list of speaker group members, it seems as if the list is not correctly managed ('Soundbar speaker' is somehow still in the list after it is removed):
```
2020-09-13 19:56:29 DEBUG (Thread-20) [pychromecast.socket_client] [Upstairs(192.168.86.213):32218] Received: Message urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.multizone from receiver-0 to *: {'deviceId': '5d5a0029-c676-4b49-57f5-82d66d28f586', 'requestId': 0, 'type': 'DEVICE_REMOVED'}
2020-09-13 19:56:29 DEBUG (Thread-20) [pychromecast.controllers.multizone] (66e85350-5adc-488c-8fe1-070458ed6556) Removed member 5d5a0029-c676-4b49-57f5-82d66d28f586(Soundbar speaker), members: {'3b26e14f-8159-802a-f4aa-49ac8fc726ad': 'Living Room home', 'c477497b-245d-bf21-f6e3-ad97320d7e15': 'Outside speaker', '4c4db197-e346-94d0-67cc-a10ffdd1212c': 'Kitchen home', '5d5a0029-c676-4b49-57f5-82d66d28f586': 'Soundbar speaker'}
2020-09-13 19:56:29 DEBUG (Thread-20) [homeassistant.components.cast.media_player] [media_player.soundbar_speaker Soundbar speaker] Multizone 66e85350-5adc-488c-8fe1-070458ed6556 media status: None
```

Edit:
This is the relevant code:
```py
    def _remove_member(self, uuid):
        name = self._members.pop(uuid, "<Unknown>")
        _LOGGER.debug(
            "(%s) Removed member %s(%s), members: %s",
            self._uuid,
            uuid,
            name,
            self._members,
        )
```
Is the formatting of the log string not done by the worker thread, if so that would explain the strange print if the _members dict is modified before the log string has been generated?

Hi @emontnemery ,

```Is the problem 100% reproducible, or does it only happen sometimes?```

Yes

```You have not by any chance blocked the ChromeCasts from updating themselves?```

Nope, standard install, Preview off, cast firmware version is 1.49.22252

I tried the following, but each attempt causes the original stream to stop and new stream to individual speaker to start

```
Start a first stream to a speaker group
Start a second stream one member of the speaker group.
The speaker group - except for the one member - should continue the first stream and a temporary group should be formed.
```

This may be as only have one account to use?
I had difficulty removing the duplicated groups, seemed to retain them after restarting HA so ended up removing from core.devices and core.entities in .storage.

> This may be as only have one account to use?

Yeah, you could try casting from another app than Spotify, or maybe with the pychromecast media example.

I had a look at the history of pychromecast and the cast component. The problem is that though we will get to know when a temporary group is formed, there's a risk that HomeAssistant misses that message.

I'm not quite sure what to do:
- Do a best effort attempt; if we get the message about the temporary group, great, we then avoid adding it to the entity registry. This would basically mean re-adding functionality removed by #33884.
- Just assume all speaker groups with same friendly name are the same, this is very error prone because several genuine groups can have the same name, groups can be renamed etc.
- Do not add speaker groups to the entity registry at all; error prone: entity id is then not stable which means automations may break etc.

Hi @emontnemery, 

It sounds like you're leaving towards the first option which makes sense, but I also think the second has merits, and a simple lookup/ defining on name would be fine. 

If people are naming speaker groups the same or in the process of renaming then temporary issues will be acceptable.
